source.title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Tom Lieberum; Nicolas Sonnerat; Arthur Conmy; Vikrant Varma; János Kramár; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: None; the text includes the full paper and appendices, despite some embedded web-page artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares SAE reconstruction fidelity across architectures and sparsity objectives, which bears on the claim that SAE error can be reduced by training choices. It does not analyze the structure or token-level predictability of the error.
record.gate_note: The reported sparsity–fidelity comparisons bear on V6. The paper does not measure linear predictability of SAE error, error scaling across SAE sizes, token overlap in errors, loss impact versus random same-size errors, or downstream behavior with and without the error term. Interpretability, feature-frequency, dead-feature, and uniformity results do not test the listed versions. No exact values for the fidelity curves are given in the text; the comparisons are described qualitatively and plotted.
record.test_reason: The study compares delta LM loss at matched L0 across SAE architectures and sparsity penalties (L0 vs L1 vs RI-L1, TopK with AuxK) on Gemma 2 9B. This bears on V6: does SAE error shrink with better training choices? It measures total reconstruction error, not dark matter decomposed into predictable and nonlinear parts. It predates the original source and is not one of them.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say JumpReLU matches or exceeds TopK fidelity, exceeds Gated fidelity at given sparsity, and is similarly interpretable. They call it a mild improvement over prevailing SAE training methods.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces and evaluates JumpReLU SAEs with an L0 penalty and straight-through estimators, comparing reconstruction fidelity across SAE architectures. It does not use the original study's dark-matter error analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction-fidelity comparisons depend on SAE architecture and sparsity level; tests cover Gemma 2 9B at layers 9, 20 and 31 and residual-stream, MLP-output and attention-output sites.
record.problems: The relevant evaluations cover a single model family, Gemma 2 9B. Fidelity comparisons are primarily presented as plots and qualitative summaries without exact reported values or uncertainty estimates. The study does not directly characterize SAE error structure or establish that most dark matter is a training artifact.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows kept for FVU curves, feature-frequency and dead-feature results, interpretability ratings, attribution-weighted sparsity, or target-L0 training: these results do not directly measure the listed claim versions. The automated interpretability analysis includes a random-initialized SAE baseline, but that result is not about SAE reconstruction-error structure.

untested.parts: Whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input; not measured.
Per-token error-norm prediction across sizes and shared failure contexts; not measured. Only one width (131k) was used.
SAE error versus random same-norm error on loss; not measured.
Linear versus nonlinear dark-matter split; not measured.
Circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term; not measured.

Untested parts: whether the reduction is in dark matter specifically; end-to-end training; whether the residual reflects model structure; whether error vanishes. Only total delta LM loss and FVU at fixed width were measured.

missing.what: Gated RI-L1 vs Gated (original L1): similar sparsity–fidelity trade-off, so changing the sparsity penalty did not reduce error (bears on V6, state absent).
Adding the AuxK dead-latent loss slightly improves TopK fidelity at given sparsity (V6, partial).
FVU-vs-L0 curves across architectures, a second error measure (Fig. 12). They were left out as not bearing on any version, but they do bear on V6.
Alternative kernels and target-L0 loss give similar fidelity, so these training choices have little effect on error.
missing.locator: Appendix F Fig. 9; Appendix H Fig. 17

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label overstates the case. The paper shows only modest architecture-driven reductions in total error and never isolates dark matter. All delta LM loss values are plot-only, from one model, Gemma 2 9B; preliminary Pythia results are mentioned but not shown. The study predates the original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes; whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts; whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and whether nonlinear error differs qualitatively or resists dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-feature analyses lose meaningful model behavior without the SAE error term.

The study compares reconstruction fidelity across SAE architectures and sparsity objectives, but does not establish that dark matter mostly reflects training artifacts, quantify its structure, compare it with end-to-end training, or show that error vanishes with better training.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B (base)
rows.operation_detail: Compare delta LM loss of SAE reconstructions at matched L0 across SAE architectures.
rows.measure: Delta LM loss at a given L0
rows.baseline: Gated (Original) at matched L0; exact value not stated
rows.value: JumpReLU consistently provides more faithful reconstructions than Gated SAEs; exact value not stated
rows.note: Qualitative comparison stated in the text; the plotted curve supplies no exact value in the text.
rows.check: The improvement over Gated is consistent, but the authors call JumpReLU only a 'mild improvement'. Error remains in every architecture and the size is only plotted, so this is not full support for V6.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V6. Better reconstruction fidelity does not establish that dark matter mostly originates in SAE training.
source_check.problem: The qualitative comparison is correct, but its interpretation as a partial observation of V6 exceeds the measurement.

relationships.condition: JumpReLU (L0 penalty) vs Gated (L1 / RI-L1), all sites and layers of Gemma 2 9B
relationships.reason: The better architecture consistently lowers delta LM loss at matched L0, but the authors call it a mild improvement and substantial error remains in all SAEs. Rows r01,r02,r04,r05,r07,r08,r10,r11,r13,r14,r16,r17,r19,r20,r22,r23,r25,r26.
relationships.display_finding: JumpReLU consistently reduced the language-model loss increase relative to Gated SAEs at matched L0, but improvements were mild and substantial reconstruction error remained.

source_check.condition: JumpReLU (L0 penalty) vs Gated (L1 / RI-L1), all sites and layers of Gemma 2 9B
source_check.reason: The cited rows establish improved fidelity, not what fraction of dark matter originates in training. The overall mild-improvement assessment and persistence of reconstruction error do not demonstrate a limitation of V6; its causal attribution remains untested.

relationships.condition: JumpReLU vs TopK (AuxK), all sites and layers
relationships.reason: Parity or a slight gain only. Removing L1 shrinkage brings little reduction relative to TopK (r03,r06,r09,r12,r15,r18,r21,r24,r27). This verdict also draws on text results with no row: switching L1 to RI-L1 left fidelity similar.
relationships.display_finding: JumpReLU matched or slightly improved on TopK fidelity; switching from L1 to RI-L1 also left fidelity similar.

labels.reason: TopK already uses no L1 sparsity penalty, so this comparison does not measure the effect of removing L1 shrinkage. Appendix D changes reparameterisation invariance and auxiliary-loss training, not L1 versus no L1. Neither result identifies the predominant origin of dark matter.

relation.reason: The paper discusses training-induced fidelity problems and evaluates architectural remedies, but does not test the predominant-origin claim in V6 or the other listed dark-matter versions.

tranche.reason: The paper evaluates its proposed SAE training method using reconstruction fidelity and interpretability. It does not distinguish whether dark matter predominantly reflects training artifacts or representation structure; ordinary method-performance comparisons do not test that attribution.

source_check.notes: The qualitative fidelity comparisons are accurately extracted; no exact curve values should be inferred. These results provide background on training sensitivity, while V6's attribution of dark matter mainly to training remains untested.

statements.correction: Gemma 2 9B base; residual-stream, MLP-output and pre-WO attention activations; layers 9, 20, 31, zero-indexed. JumpReLU exceeds Gated fidelity and matches or exceeds TopK fidelity at matched sparsity. Overall methodology assessed as a mild improvement. Predominant origin of residual error untested.
statements.problem: The architecture comparisons and Gemma conditions are correct. The authors' mild-improvement assessment concerns the overall methodology, including efficiency and interpretability. The text does not establish that the remaining error is substantial in a sense that limits V6, or attribute it to representation structure.

statements.correction: JumpReLU consistently improves fidelity over Gated and matches or often slightly improves upon TopK across the tested Gemma sites. Mild improvement is the authors' overall assessment of JumpReLU training methodology.
statements.problem: The direction of the comparisons is correct, but mild describes the overall methodology rather than a quantified fidelity gain over Gated. These comparisons do not determine the source of dark matter.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: JumpReLU compared with Gated (Original) and Gated (RI-L1) at matched L0 across the tested Gemma 2 9B sites and layers
reader_labels.reason: JumpReLU is reported to achieve more faithful reconstructions than Gated SAEs at a given sparsity, showing that SAE architecture/training choice changes reconstruction error (r01-r02, r04-r05, r07-r08, r10-r11, r13-r14, r16-r17, r19-r20, r22-r23, r25-r26).
